newsitem.title: ITALY: Dini backs Italian budget but seeks some changes.
newsitem.headline: Dini backs Italian budget but seeks some changes.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, who is head of government coalition party Italian Renewal, said on Tuesday that he supported the 1997 budget but his group would try to introduce some amendments to the package when it went before parliament.
Italian Renewal's leader in the lower house of parliament, Diego Masi, resigned from his post in protest over the draft budget last Friday.

But Dini said his party as a whole supported the budget, which is designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit and put Italy into the first wave of countries signing up to the single European currency.

"We reserve the right to present amendments to correct some points of fiscal measures," Dini told reporters. "But we share the global objectives and they can bring us very close to the parameters required to enter into Europe."
Prodi's centre-left government is due to officially present the budget to parliament on Thursday where tough opposition awaits.
Dini said "I think the governing majority is compact and has the votes to get the budget passed."
Prodi's Olive Tree coalition has a majority in the Senate (upper house) but relies on support from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party in the lower Chamber of Deputies.
Parliament has until the end of the year to ratify the budget. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
